items.title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
items.content_text: Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately. The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago, and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. items.title: Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks
items.content_text: Nvidia's board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. The decision was unanimous, Nvidia said in a press release, following talks with Huang and feedback from senior US government officials who concluded that his return poses no national security risk. The Riemann Hypothesis is widely considered the most intellectually demanding unsolved problem in mathematics. The brightest minds have failed to crack it for 150 years. items.title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now
items.content_text: Paradromics has announced a strategic partnership with Nvidia to utilize the latter's AI hardware and software stack to miniaturize brain signal decoding systems. The collaboration focuses on replacing current bulky, cart-based electronics with portable terminal devices, leveraging edge computing to process massive neural datasets in real-time.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra solved a math theorem no other AI could crack, then invented its own proof strategy
items.content_text: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra model successfully generated a machine-verifiable proof for the Smoktunowicz gap theorem on the Autoform-Hard benchmark, overcoming missing mathematical foundations in the library. By autonomously selecting a new research-based proof strategy, the model produced 1,800 lines of Lean code, signaling a transition from heuristic searching to creative proof generation in AI reasoning.

items.title: Marlowe Raises $277 Million to Bolster Alternatives to Nvidia Chips
items.content_text: AI infrastructure startup Marlowe has secured $277 million in funding to develop compute infrastructure utilizing AMD accelerators as an alternative to Nvidia hardware. The company plans to deploy its first data center by the end of 2026, aiming to challenge Nvidia's market dominance.

items.title: Bret Taylor’s Sierra Finalizing More Than $1.75 Billion Round
items.content_text: Customer service AI startup Sierra, founded by Bret Taylor, is finalizing a funding round exceeding $1.75 billion, led by Lightspeed and Greenoaks. The transaction values the company at $30 billion, up from $15.8 billion in May, reflecting intense investor confidence in AI-driven enterprise service automation.

Will it bring on total societal collapse? Though there’s room for disagreement about which catastrophe is most salient, experts are aligned on the idea that society is, for one reason or another, in real trouble. items.title: How Nvidia fought for years in Washington to sell its prized chips to China
items.content_text: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's political influence has collapsed following revelations of his involvement with a woman suspected of espionage for China, whose firm is under investigation for illicit trade of Nvidia chips. Previously, Nvidia employed aggressive lobbying to circumvent export restrictions and resisted mandatory chip-tracking regulations by claiming compliance was technically impossible, causing severe backlash and deep distrust among U.S. lawmakers.

items.title: US ports face cyber attack onslaught as hackers target vital trade routes
items.content_text: Kent Britton, CEO of the Port of Corpus Christi, reported that the port faces thousands of daily network intrusion attempts. The FBI has warned that malicious actors are increasingly deploying an AI tool dubbed 'Artex' to automate the exploitation of software vulnerabilities within ports and shipping infrastructure, shifting from password spraying to sophisticated executive phishing.

items.title: Meta Muse can now do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart
items.content_text: Walmart has integrated Meta’s Muse AI agent through its recently announced Agent Gateway. Customers can authorize Muse via 'Agent Profiles' to autonomously browse and purchase products, with built-in spending limits, manual approval requirements, and privacy protections to prevent purchase history leakage.

items.title: States Sue SpaceX Over Grok Deepfakes
items.content_text: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing Elon Musk’s SpaceX, alleging that the company violated consumer protection laws by lying to users about both the safety of its generative AI tools and how seriously the company took stopping child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and nonconsensual intimate imagery (NCII) from proliferating on its platforms. items.title: Why using rocks for carbon removal could eventually reduce crop growth
items.content_text: Research by CarbonPlan suggests that 'Enhanced Rock Weathering' (ERW), a climate solution heavily backed by Google and Microsoft, faces significant scalability challenges. The study indicates that spreading basalt or olivine at levels required for climate impact may degrade soil health and decrease crop yields; scaling back applications to protect harvests would likely cap the method's CO2 removal potential to under 1 billion tons per year.

items.title: Crowdstrike Reaches 44 Billion Cybersecurity Deal For Zscaler
items.content_text: CrowdStrike has entered an all-stock acquisition agreement to purchase Zscaler in a deal valued at approximately $43.9 billion. The merger combines CrowdStrike’s endpoint security with Zscaler’s zero-trust network offerings to meet enterprise demand for vendor consolidation, with Zscaler shareholders receiving 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, resulting in existing CrowdStrike shareholders owning 84.1% of the new entity.

items.title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, a 750B-parameter flagship model built on its Loop Transformer architecture, reaching intelligence levels comparable to 2T-3T models (Z.ai)
items.content_text: Z.ai has launched its flagship model, GLM-5.4, utilizing the proprietary 'Loop Transformer' architecture. By scaling loop depth alongside total parameter size, the 750B-parameter model achieves performance benchmarks comparable to 2T-3T scale models, signaling a significant breakthrough in architectural efficiency.

items.title: Ex-Sequoia Boss Backs UK Defense Startup at $450 Million Value
items.content_text: European defense AI startup Agon has raised $70 million in a Series A round, valuing the firm at $450 million to develop foundational infrastructure for agentic warfare. The round, led by Northzone, marks the first joint investment from the UK Sovereign AI Fund and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund, with participation from former Sequoia global leader Roelof Botha.

items.title: Trump hosts crypto traders as demand for his meme coin fades
items.content_text: Former U.S. President Donald Trump hosted a crypto investor reception at his Northern Virginia golf club, aiming to re-engage high-net-worth holders and revive the market interest in his meme coins. Trump explicitly called for Congress to enact a federal regulatory framework for digital assets, attempting to align his political agenda with the industry's push for legal clarity.

items.title: Behind China’s A.I. Anxieties, Fear of a Nuclear Checkmate
items.content_text: Researchers at the Academy of Military Science in Beijing warn that the U.S. integration of AI into nuclear decision-making could compress response times from 15-30 minutes to under 90 seconds. This capability sparks concerns that U.S. forces may achieve superior precision in detecting and neutralizing Chinese nuclear assets, thereby undermining Beijing's second-strike deterrence.

items.title: Governors Call for Federal AI Rules Without Sidelining States
items.content_text: California Governor Gavin Newsom released a framework for AI governance, proposing baseline safety standards, mandatory third-party audits, emergency shutdown authorities, and limits on recursive self-improvement. The initiative aims to fill federal regulatory voids by imposing legal oversight on AI models with extreme catastrophic risk potential.

items.title: Boston-based Aevius, whose foundation models analyze patient health using medical records, imaging, and other data, raised a $22M seed led by Insight Partners (Katherine Davis/Axios)
items.content_text: Clinical intelligence startup Aevius has raised $22 million in seed funding led by Insight Partners. The founding team, leveraging their successful track record in selling clinical AI assets to Big Pharma, will focus on building foundation models that analyze EHRs, medical imaging, and multi-modal health data.

items.title: Compute Desk, which is building capital markets infrastructure to price, trade, hedge, and clear compute, raised a $45M seed round led by Lightspeed (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
items.content_text: Compute Desk raised $45 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Led by CEO Andrawes Bahou, the startup aims to build capital markets infrastructure to turn compute into a tradable, hedgeable asset, addressing the growing financialization of AI hardware resources.
